title: Anomaly Detection
html:
Anomaly detection finds rows that don't look like the rest — fraud, intrusions, faulty sensors, manufacturing defects. Labels are usually scarce, so most methods learn what normal looks like and score deviations from it.

KindExample
Point anomalyA $9,000 purchase on a card that averages $40
Contextual anomaly30 °C is normal in July, anomalous in January
Collective anomalyA burst of small logins from one IP, each normal on its own

Approaches

ApproachMethodIdea
Statisticalz-score, IQR, robust z-score (median/MAD)Far from the centre of one feature's distribution
IsolationIsolationForestRandom splits isolate anomalies in fewer steps (shorter tree paths)
Density / distanceLocalOutlierFactor, k-NN distanceMuch lower local density than the neighbours
BoundaryOneClassSVMA boundary enclosing the normal data
ReconstructionPCA, autoencodersNormal data compresses well; anomalies reconstruct badly
SupervisedAny classifier with class weightsWhen enough labelled anomalies exist — usually the most accurate
robust z = 0.6745 · (x − median) / MAD flag if |robust z| > 3.5 (MAD = median |x − median|)

Isolation Forest and LOF

contamination sets the expected share of anomalies — it only moves the threshold on the anomaly score (score_samples / decision_function). In practice, rank rows by score and review the top k.

Practical notes

  • Outlier detection (training data contains anomalies) vs novelty detection (train on clean data, score new points — LocalOutlierFactor(novelty=True), OneClassSVM).
  • Evaluate with whatever labels exist: precision@k (analysts review k alerts a day), recall on known incidents, PR-AUC. Accuracy is meaningless when 99.9% of rows are normal.
  • Scale features for distance-based methods; Isolation Forest doesn't need it.
  • Once labelled anomalies accumulate, a supervised model (often gradient boosting with class weights) usually beats unsupervised scores — or use the scores as features for it.
  • Attackers adapt: monitor and retrain (see Deployment, Monitoring & MLOps).
How does Isolation Forest work?

It builds random trees that split on a random feature at a random threshold. Anomalies are few and different, so they are isolated near the root — their average path length across trees is short — while normal points need many splits. The anomaly score is based on that average path length.

How do you evaluate an anomaly detector without labels?

Get at least a small labelled sample (analyst review of the top-scored and a random set of rows), then measure precision@k and recall. Also check stability of scores over time and use synthetic injected anomalies as a sanity check.
